subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm aiming for a reasonably sized model with over 150 parts and a few textures, keeping the code economical but correct. For the vehicle, I'm deciding to skip a full creature skeleton and instead use a handful of simple joints for the turret, gun elevation, and stabilizer legs rather than building a complex rig.

I'm sketching the proportions: an 8-wheel truck around 10m long and 3m wide, with the chassis stretching from z -5 to 5, a cab up front, and a rail-gun mount on the rear deck firing forward over the cab at a slight elevation, giving a total height near 3.5m including the barrel. I'm also planning four deployable outrigger stabilizer legs that extend sideways and down to brace against the ground, using simple box geometry helpers with flat metallic colors, and considering pulling in a glow kit for added visual effect.

Now I'm working through decal and paint ideas like camo patches, hazard stripes, a star emblem, and warning labels, then moving into the actual joint hierarchy: a hull joint, a turret joint rotating on the vertical axis, and a gun cradle joint angled for barrel elevation, with the barrel built as a rod extending along a computed direction vector. I'm also laying out the wheel axle positions along the chassis length for a three-axle-per-side configuration.

Still deciding wheel placements...

Planning the hull as a lower chassis box with an upper deck, using panelled camo paneling for armored side skirts, then shifting to the cab front with an extruded wedge shape for the armored nose.

Working out the cab's angled profile for a sharp wedge silhouette, sized to a 2.4 width and positioned forward on the hull, then roughing in slanted dark-glass windshield panels using thin tilted boxes to suggest glazing without a separate texture.

Still need radar/sensor masts, antennas, cab lights, headlight glow, exhaust stacks, fuel tanks, and side tool boxes to round out the detailing.

Now I'm working on the railgun itself: two parallel steel rails with a glowing blue gap between them, a breech block, ringed shroud segments along the barrel, and a muzzle brake, all oriented along the barrel's forward direction using a helper function to position points relative to the gun's local axes.

I'm checking that the barrel's elevation and length keep its tip clear of the cab roof and hull, adjusting the pivot height and adding trunnion support structures like a turret ring base and side cheek boxes to hold the barrel in place.

Now I'm working out the four stabiliser legs: positioning them outward from the chassis beyond the wheels, with horizontal beams, downward hydraulic cylinders, diagonal braces, and ribbed circular pads touching the ground, along with the joints connecting each leg to the hull.

Rear leg beam placement at z -4.0 near the chassis end works fine. Now I'm planning the color palette (olive, dark, tan, steel, glow blue, orange hazard) and the decal textures I'll need: hazard stripes for the stabilizer pads, a circular "RC-6" emblem decal for the side panels, a "HIGH VOLTAGE" warning label with a bolt icon, and a camera-related texture.

I'm also deciding on a number plate reading "PLA-07," a glowing waveform display texture for the capacitor bank screen, and a procedural tire paint — using normal direction and UV coordinates to distinguish the sidewall from the tread so I can alternate tread block patterns around the cylinder.

For details I'm planning cab door emblem decals as thin planes facing outward on each side, antenna rods, and a radar dish built from a partial sphere geometry to mimic a lathe shape, keeping part count low by skipping unnecessary geometry merges.

Now I'm defining helper functions for building box parts with sensible default bone attachment to the nearest joint, with explicit overrides for turret and gun pieces. I'm laying out the joint hierarchy—hull, turret, gun, and wheel joints named by position (FL, ML, RL, etc.)—parented appropriately so the rig drives the tank's hull, turret rotation, and wheel placement correctly.

Turning to turret details now: adding a turret ring, cheek plates, trunnion cylinders for the gun pivot, a cradle/breech box, recoil buffer cylinders, and the rail assembly geometry along the gun barrel.

Still placing geometry blocks...

Checking toolbox placement between the wheel axles to avoid clashing with the leg beams, fitting it around z -1.1 at x 1.45. I'm reconsidering the fuel tank's position since it conflicts with a leg beam, so I'll skip the tank and adjust the beam height instead.

Now I'm positioning fenders over each wheel using small boxes that overlap slightly with the hull edge, adding axle rods across the chassis at each axle height, and placing differential housing spheres at the centers. I'm also working out headlight glow box placement at the cab front, figuring out the right y-coordinate relative to the cab's base height.

Working out cab geometry now, computing the roof height from the deck top plus cab height, and figuring the front slope profile from the base vertical face up to the roof angle. I'm placing the bumper box and headlights relative to the cab front z-position, then working out the windshield slope coordinates by transforming local profile points into world space to find the midpoint and orientation.

Computing glass normal vectors...

Still writing gun placement helpers...

Now setting up wheel joints per side and row, attaching tire cylinders, hub, rim, and bolt details around each wheel.

Writing tire paint and stabiliser joints...

Still placing geometry details...

Adding capacitor can cylinders glowing on top of the bank, then positioning turret cheek plates flanking the gun near the top of the turret.

Now I'm placing the gun's pivot trunnions as cylinders at the turret joint, adding a breech housing box in dark steel/olive, and setting up recoil cylinders on either side of the gun. I'm also linking elevation hydraulic rods between the turret mounting points and the gun body to simulate the recoil mechanism.

I'm sketching out the decal SVGs next: hazard stripes using a yellow background with black diagonal path strokes, an emblem with a star and outline, a dark glowing waveform screen, a yellow warning triangle with a bolt icon, and a plate labeled "RG-06," all kept under the color limit for efficiency.

Now I'm figuring out placement: putting the emblem on the cab doors instead of the hull sides since wheels and toolboxes block those spots, placing the plate on the front bumper, and adding a small hazard decal to the hull skirt. I also need to double-check wheel and pad positioning so nothing clips below the ground plane.
